newsitem.title: USA: Osmonics sees efficiencies from new system.
newsitem.headline: Osmonics sees efficiencies from new system.

text.p: Osmonics Inc said Tuesday it expected costs of a new management information system to pressure earnings for the full year, but it said expense cuts and efficiencies should help improve operating results.

"This month we went live on the new SAP management information system in Minnetonka and Syracuse, which affects about half of the corporate employees," Chairman and Chief Executive D. Dean Spatz said in a statement.

"The SAP conversion has been expensive, and we expended about two cents per share in the second quarter for the transition," Spatz said. "We now estimate the total SAP transition expense will be five to six cents per share for all of 1997."
Earlier Osmonics, which makes water purification products, said it earned $2.6 million, or $0.18 a share, in the second quarter, compared to $3.1 million, or $0.21, a year earlier.

The company said it believes it can improve gross margins "somewhat more" by expanding its cellular manufacturing and focused factories. It also said expense cuts and efficiences from the SAP system would allow it to improve operating income to historical levels.
